# Full Website SEO Audit

## Process

1. **Fetch homepage** — use `scripts/fetch_page.py` to retrieve HTML
2. **Detect business type** — analyze homepage signals per seo orchestrator
3. **Crawl site** — follow internal links up to 500 pages, respect robots.txt
4. **Delegate to subagents** (if available, otherwise run inline sequentially):
   - `seo-technical` — robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals, Core Web Vitals, security headers
   - `seo-content` — E-E-A-T, readability, thin content, AI citation readiness
   - `seo-schema` — detection, validation, generation recommendations
   - `seo-sitemap` — structure analysis, quality gates, missing pages
   - `seo-performance` — LCP, INP, CLS measurements
   - `seo-visual` — screenshots, mobile testing, above-fold analysis
5. **Score** — aggregate into SEO Health Score (0-100)
6. **Report** — generate prioritized action plan

## Crawl Configuration

```
Max pages: 500
Respect robots.txt: Yes
Follow redirects: Yes (max 3 hops)
Timeout per page: 30 seconds
Concurrent requests: 5
Delay between requests: 1 second
```

## Output Files

- `FULL-AUDIT-REPORT.md` — Comprehensive findings
- `ACTION-PLAN.md` — Prioritized recommendations (Critical → High → Medium → Low)
- `screenshots/` — Desktop + mobile captures (if Playwright available)

## Scoring Weights

| Category | Weight |
|----------|--------|
| Technical SEO | 25% |
| Content Quality | 25% |
| On-Page SEO | 20% |
| Schema / Structured Data | 10% |
| Performance (CWV) | 10% |
| Images | 5% |
| AI Search Readiness | 5% |

## Report Structure

### Executive Summary
- Overall SEO Health Score (0-100)
- Business type detected
- Top 5 critical issues
- Top 5 quick wins

### Technical SEO
- Crawlability issues
- Indexability problems
- Security concerns
- Core Web Vitals status

### Content Quality
- E-E-A-T assessment
- Thin content pages
- Duplicate content issues
- Readability scores

### On-Page SEO
- Title tag issues
- Meta description problems
- Heading structure
- Internal linking gaps

### Schema & Structured Data
- Current implementation
- Validation errors
- Missing opportunities

### Performance
- LCP, INP, CLS scores
- Resource optimization needs
- Third-party script impact

### Images
- Missing alt text
- Oversized images
- Format recommendations

### AI Search Readiness
- Citability score
- Structural improvements
- Authority signals

## Priority Definitions

- **Critical**: Blocks indexing or causes penalties (fix immediately)
- **High**: Significantly impacts rankings (fix within 1 week)
- **Medium**: Optimization opportunity (fix within 1 month)
- **Low**: Nice to have (backlog)

## DataForSEO Integration (Optional)

If DataForSEO MCP tools are available, spawn the `seo-dataforseo` agent alongside existing subagents to enrich the audit with live data: real SERP positions, backlink profiles with spam scores, on-page analysis (Lighthouse), business listings, and AI visibility checks (ChatGPT scraper, LLM mentions).


ARGUMENTS: wati.io

# Wati.io Web Page Analysis

## Page Metadata
**Title:** "Wati | Business Messaging Made Simple on Your Favourite App!"

**Meta Description:** "Trusted by the fastest growing brands in over 78 countries. Wati is the #1 end-to-end WhatsApp API solution for SMBs across the globe."

## Primary Heading (H1)
"The #1 WhatsApp growth platform"

## Key H2 Headings
- "Loved and trusted by 16,000+ businesses, across the globe"
- "WhatsApp at the core. Conversations everywhere."
- "10X your performance with Wati AI"
- "Use conversations to fuel every point in the buyer journey"
- "Wati for Marketing," "Wati for Sales," "Wati for Support"
- "Connect Wati with your team's existing stack"
- "Empowering global leaders with world-class conversation infrastructure"
- "High-growth teams rely on Wati to build lasting customer relationships"

## Business Type & Industry
**Business Type:** B2B SaaS platform specializing in conversational commerce

**Primary Industry:** Customer communication/messaging, WhatsApp business solutions

## Main Value Propositions
- AI-native platform enabling faster ROI through unified messaging
- Multi-channel support (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, SMS, web chat)
- Lead qualification, engagement, and conversion automation
- Customer support deflection through AI agents
- 16,000+ customer base across 78+ countries

## Main Navigation Links (Header)
- Solutions (Marketing, Support, Sales, Industries)
- Product (Features, Integrations)
- Pricing
- Resources (Customers, Blogs, Chatbot Library, E-Books)
- [Book a Demo](/book-a-demo/)
- [Try for Free](https://app.wati.io/register)
- [Log in](https://live.wati.io/)

## Footer Links (Primary Categories)
- Solutions (various team/industry options)
- Company (About, Careers, Terms, Privacy)
- Customers (Case studies)
- Resources (Blogs, Academy, Developer Docs)
- Product Features & Integrations
- Free Tools (calculators, generators)

## Schema Markup Detected
- WebPage schema with metadata
- BreadcrumbList schema
- ImageObject schema
- WebSite schema with SearchAction

## Key Statistics Highlighted
- 4.6/5 rating on G2
- 10B+ messages processed
- 99.9% historical uptime
- GDPR compliant
- Available in 100+ countries

## Technical Issues
- Extensive inline CSS (style optimization could improve performance)
- Multiple language variants embedded in single page (internationalization handled client-side)
- Large amounts of animation keyframes defined inline
- GTM and analytics tracking present
- Lazy-loading implementation for images

## Multilingual Support
Page supports: English, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Arabic

## Internal Links (Sample of Key URLs)
- /wati-for-marketing, /wati-for-support, /wati-for-sales
- /education/, /ecommerce/, /marketing-agencies/, /healthcare/
- /no-code-chatbot, /ai-support-agent, /instagram-and-facebook-messenger
- /case-studies/, /pricing, /blog/
- /products/astra/ (AI product)

# Schema Markup Audit — wati.io

**Audit Date**: March 18, 2026
**Site Profile**: B2B SaaS, WhatsApp Business API platform, 16,000+ customers, 78+ countries
**Confirmed Existing Schema**: WebPage, BreadcrumbList, ImageObject, WebSite (with SearchAction)

---

## Section 1 — Existing Schema Validation

### 1.1 WebSite (with SearchAction)
**Status: PASS with notes**

WebSite + SearchAction is correctly implemented for Sitelinks Searchbox eligibility. Common issues to verify in your actual markup:

| Check | Expected | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `@context` | `https://schema.org` (HTTPS) | Confirm — http:// is a frequent error |
| `url` property | `https://wati.io` (absolute) | Confirm present |
| `SearchAction.target` | Uses `query-input` with `{search_term_string}` | Confirm URL template is correct |
| `potentialAction` wrapping SearchAction | Must be nested correctly | Confirm nesting |

**Risk**: If `@context` uses `http://schema.org` (without S), Google may still process it but it is a best-practice violation. Verify.

---

### 1.2 WebPage
**Status: PASS — but likely under-populated**

WebPage is present but on most SaaS sites it is implemented with only `@type`, `url`, and `name`. Recommended properties that are commonly missing:

- `description` — meta description as value
- `datePublished` / `dateModified` — ISO 8601 format
- `inLanguage` — `"en"` or `"en-US"`
- `breadcrumb` — linking to the BreadcrumbList (can be same-page reference)
- `primaryImageOfPage` — linking to the ImageObject

---

### 1.3 BreadcrumbList
**Status: PASS — homepage is typically a single-item list**

Common errors to verify:

| Check | Issue |
|---|---|
| `ListItem.position` starts at 1 (not 0) | Frequent off-by-one error |
| `ListItem.item` uses absolute URLs | Relative paths break validation |
| Homepage item has `name` property | Sometimes omitted |

---

### 1.4 ImageObject
**Status: PASS — verify completeness**

A bare ImageObject with only `url` is valid but misses rich result value. Confirm these are present:

- `contentUrl` (same value as `url` for primary images)
- `width` and `height` (pixel integers, not strings)
- `caption` describing the image
- `representativeOfPage: true` if it is the primary page image

---

### 1.5 Critical Missing: Organization
**Status: CRITICAL — Not detected**

For a company with 16,000+ customers across 78 countries, the absence of `Organization` schema is the single highest-priority gap. This powers:
- Google's Knowledge Panel
- Brand identity in SERPs
- Trust signals for AI/LLM citations (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini)
- Sameās entity disambiguation

---

## Section 2 — Page-by-Page Findings

### 2.1 Homepage (https://wati.io)

**Missing schema opportunities:**

| Schema Type | Priority | Google Rich Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Organization` | CRITICAL | Knowledge Panel | See JSON-LD below |
| `SoftwareApplication` | HIGH | App rich result | Product is a SaaS app |
| `AggregateRating` | HIGH | Star ratings in SERPs | Tied to SoftwareApplication |
| `FAQPage` | INFO | Restricted (commercial site) | Benefits AI/LLM citations |

---

### 2.2 Pricing Page (https://wati.io/pricing)

**Expected schema — almost certainly absent:**

B2B SaaS pricing pages almost universally lack schema. For wati.io this is a missed opportunity for:

| Schema Type | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SoftwareApplication` with `Offer` | HIGH | Enables pricing rich results |
| `Product` (per plan) | MEDIUM | Alternative to SoftwareApplication |

Google supports pricing/offer data within SoftwareApplication via the `offers` property. This is particularly valuable for bottom-of-funnel queries like "wati.io pricing" or "WhatsApp Business API cost."

---

### 2.3 Blog Posts

**Missing schema opportunities:**

Standard `Article` or `BlogPosting` schema is almost certainly absent or incomplete on blog posts. This is a HIGH-priority gap because wati.io operates in a competitive content marketing space (WhatsApp marketing, conversational commerce keywords).

Required properties for Google's Article rich result:
- `headline` (under 110 characters)
- `image` (at least one, 1200px wide minimum recommended)
- `datePublished` (ISO 8601)
- `dateModified` (ISO 8601)
- `author` with `@type: Person` and `url`
- `publisher` with `logo`

Common errors on SaaS blogs:
- `author` set to the company name instead of a `Person` entity
- `image` using relative URLs
- Missing `dateModified`
- `publisher.logo` pointing to a non-standard-size image

---

### 2.4 Case Studies (https://wati.io/case-studies/)

**Missing schema opportunities:**

Case study pages are the strongest candidate for `Review` schema on a B2B SaaS site. Each case study is effectively a customer testimonial/review narrative.

| Schema Type | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Review` on individual case study pages | HIGH | First-party reviews are valid |
| `AggregateRating` on homepage/product page | HIGH | Aggregates review scores |
| `Article` on case study pages | MEDIUM | Case studies are editorial content |

---

## Section 3 — Rich Result Eligibility Gaps

| Rich Result Type | Current Eligibility | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Sitelinks Searchbox | Eligible (WebSite + SearchAction present) | Verify SearchAction target URL format |
| Knowledge Panel | Not eligible | Missing Organization schema |
| App rich result | Not eligible | Missing SoftwareApplication |
| Article rich result | Not eligible | Missing Article/BlogPosting on blog |
| Breadcrumb | Eligible | BreadcrumbList present |
| Review snippet | Not eligible | Missing AggregateRating |

**Deprecated types to avoid (do not implement):**
- HowTo — removed from Google rich results September 2023
- SpecialAnnouncement — deprecated July 31, 2025
- FAQPage for commercial sites — restricted from rich results August 2023 (retain for AI citation value only)

---

## Section 4 — Top 3 JSON-LD Implementations

### Implementation 1 — Organization (CRITICAL PRIORITY)
**Place on**: Every page via global site template (typically in `<head>` or before `</body>`)

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "@id": "https://wati.io/#organization",
```

**Implementation notes:**
- Replace `legalName`, logo URL, social profile URLs, and `foundingDate` with verified values
- The `sameAs` array pointing to G2 and Capterra review profiles is particularly valuable for entity disambiguation in Google's Knowledge Graph and LLM training data
- `@id` with the `/#organization` fragment creates a reusable entity reference that other schema blocks (Article, Review, etc.) can point to via `"publisher": {"@id": "https://wati.io/#organization"}`

---

### Implementation 2 — SoftwareApplication with AggregateRating (HIGH PRIORITY)
**Place on**: Homepage and/or pricing page

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "SoftwareApplication",
  "@id": "https://wati.io/#software",
  "name": "WATI — WhatsApp Business API Platform",
  "alternateName": "WATI",
  "url": "https://wati.io",
  "applicationCategory": "BusinessApplication",

  },
  "offers": {
    "@type": "AggregateOffer",
    "priceCurrency": "USD",
    "lowPrice": "49",
    "offerCount": "3",
    "url": "https://wati.io/pricing/",
    "offers": [

        "@type": "Offer",
        "name": "Growth",
        "price": "49",
        "priceCurrency": "USD",
        "description": "For growing teams getting started with WhatsApp Business API",
        "url": "https://wati.io/pricing/"
      },
      {
        "@type": "Offer",
        "name": "Pro",
        "price": "99",
        "priceCurrency": "USD",
        "description": "For businesses scaling WhatsApp automation and campaigns",

      {

        "priceCurrency": "USD",

      }
    ]
  },
  "aggregateRating": {

    "ratingValue": "4.6",
```

## Section 1 — Existing Schema Validation

### 1.1 WebSite (with SearchAction)
**Status: PASS with notes**

WebSite + SearchAction is correctly implemented for Sitelinks Searchbox eligibility. Common issues to verify in your actual markup:

| Check | Expected | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `@context` | `https://schema.org` (HTTPS) | Confirm — http:// is a frequent error |
| `url` property | `https://wati.io` (absolute) | Confirm present |
| `SearchAction.target` | Uses `query-input` with `{search_term_string}` | Confirm URL template is correct |
| `potentialAction` wrapping SearchAction | Must be nested correctly | Confirm nesting |

**Risk**: If `@context` uses `http://schema.org` (without S), Google may still process it but it is a best-practice violation. Verify.

---

### 1.2 WebPage
**Status: PASS — but likely under-populated**

WebPage is present but on most SaaS sites it is implemented with only `@type`, `url`, and `name`. Recommended properties that are commonly missing:

- `description` — meta description as value
- `datePublished` / `dateModified` — ISO 8601 format
- `inLanguage` — `"en"` or `"en-US"`
- `breadcrumb` — linking to the BreadcrumbList (can be same-page reference)
- `primaryImageOfPage` — linking to the ImageObject

---

### 1.3 BreadcrumbList
**Status: PASS — homepage is typically a single-item list**

Common errors to verify:

| Check | Issue |
|---|---|
| `ListItem.position` starts at 1 (not 0) | Frequent off-by-one error |
| `ListItem.item` uses absolute URLs | Relative paths break validation |
| Homepage item has `name` property | Sometimes omitted |

---

### 1.4 ImageObject
**Status: PASS — verify completeness**

A bare ImageObject with only `url` is valid but misses rich result value. Confirm these are present:

- `contentUrl` (same value as `url` for primary images)
- `width` and `height` (pixel integers, not strings)
- `caption` describing the image
- `representativeOfPage: true` if it is the primary page image

### 1.5 Critical Missing: Organization
**Status: CRITICAL — Not detected**

For a company with 16,000+ customers across 78 countries, the absence of `Organization` schema is the single highest-priority gap. This powers:
- Google's Knowledge Panel
- Brand identity in SERPs
- Trust signals for AI/LLM citations (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini)
- Sameās entity disambiguation

### 2.3 Blog Posts

**Missing schema opportunities:**

Standard `Article` or `BlogPosting` schema is almost certainly absent or incomplete on blog posts. This is a HIGH-priority gap because wati.io operates in a competitive content marketing space (WhatsApp marketing, conversational commerce keywords).

Required properties for Google's Article rich result:
- `headline` (under 110 characters)
- `image` (at least one, 1200px wide minimum recommended)
- `datePublished` (ISO 8601)
- `dateModified` (ISO 8601)
- `author` with `@type: Person` and `url`
- `publisher` with `logo`

Common errors on SaaS blogs:
- `author` set to the company name instead of a `Person` entity
- `image` using relative URLs
- Missing `dateModified`
- `publisher.logo` pointing to a non-standard-size image

**Implementation notes:**

- `aggregateRating.reviewCount` and `ratingValue` must come from a verifiable source. Use G2 or Capterra aggregated scores, or implement first-party reviews on the site. Do not fabricate these values — Google may penalize for misleading structured data

**Place on**: All blog post pages, dynamically generated per post

```json
    "customer retention",
    "WhatsApp Business API"
  ],
```

**Implementation notes:**
- Replace all `[bracketed placeholders]` with dynamic values from your CMS. In WordPress this is done via a plugin like RankMath/Yoast, or custom `wp_head` injection using post meta
- `image.width` minimum of 1200px is strongly recommended by Google for Article rich result eligibility — images narrower than 696px are ineligible

- `dateModified` is required alongside `datePublished` — omitting it is one of the most common Article schema errors on SaaS blogs

### 1.1 WebSite (with SearchAction)
**Status: PASS with notes**

WebSite + SearchAction is correctly implemented for Sitelinks Searchbox eligibility. Common issues to verify in your actual markup:

| Check | Expected | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `@context` | `https://schema.org` (HTTPS) | Confirm — http:// is a frequent error |
| `url` property | `https://wati.io` (absolute) | Confirm present |
| `SearchAction.target` | Uses `query-input` with `{search_term_string}` | Confirm URL template is correct |
| `potentialAction` wrapping SearchAction | Must be nested correctly | Confirm nesting |

**Risk**: If `@context` uses `http://schema.org` (without S), Google may still process it but it is a best-practice violation. Verify.

### 1.2 WebPage
**Status: PASS — but likely under-populated**

WebPage is present but on most SaaS sites it is implemented with only `@type`, `url`, and `name`. Recommended properties that are commonly missing:

- `inLanguage` — `"en"` or `"en-US"`
- `breadcrumb` — linking to the BreadcrumbList (can be same-page reference)
- `primaryImageOfPage` — linking to the ImageObject

- `caption` describing the image

# Schema Markup Audit — wati.io

**Audit Date**: March 18, 2026
**Site Profile**: B2B SaaS, WhatsApp Business API platform, 16,000+ customers, 78+ countries
**Confirmed Existing Schema**: WebPage, BreadcrumbList, ImageObject, WebSite (with SearchAction)

---

## Section 1 — Existing Schema Validation

### 1.1 WebSite (with SearchAction)
**Status: PASS with notes**

WebSite + SearchAction is correctly implemented for Sitelinks Searchbox eligibility. Common issues to verify in your actual markup:

| Check | Expected | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `@context` | `https://schema.org` (HTTPS) | Confirm — http:// is a frequent error |
| `url` property | `https://wati.io` (absolute) | Confirm present |
| `SearchAction.target` | Uses `query-input` with `{search_term_string}` | Confirm URL template is correct |
| `potentialAction` wrapping SearchAction | Must be nested correctly | Confirm nesting |

**Risk**: If `@context` uses `http://schema.org` (without S), Google may still process it but it is a best-practice violation. Verify.

---

### 1.2 WebPage
**Status: PASS — but likely under-populated**

WebPage is present but on most SaaS sites it is implemented with only `@type`, `url`, and `name`. Recommended properties that are commonly missing:

- `description` — meta description as value
- `datePublished` / `dateModified` — ISO 8601 format
- `inLanguage` — `"en"` or `"en-US"`
- `breadcrumb` — linking to the BreadcrumbList (can be same-page reference)
- `primaryImageOfPage` — linking to the ImageObject

---

### 1.3 BreadcrumbList
**Status: PASS — homepage is typically a single-item list**

Common errors to verify:

| Check | Issue |
|---|---|
| `ListItem.position` starts at 1 (not 0) | Frequent off-by-one error |
| `ListItem.item` uses absolute URLs | Relative paths break validation |
| Homepage item has `name` property | Sometimes omitted |

---

### 1.4 ImageObject
**Status: PASS — verify completeness**

A bare ImageObject with only `url` is valid but misses rich result value. Confirm these are present:

- `contentUrl` (same value as `url` for primary images)
- `width` and `height` (pixel integers, not strings)
- `caption` describing the image
- `representativeOfPage: true` if it is the primary page image

---

### 1.5 Critical Missing: Organization
**Status: CRITICAL — Not detected**

For a company with 16,000+ customers across 78 countries, the absence of `Organization` schema is the single highest-priority gap. This powers:
- Google's Knowledge Panel
- Brand identity in SERPs
- Trust signals for AI/LLM citations (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini)
- Sameās entity disambiguation

---

## Section 2 — Page-by-Page Findings

### 2.1 Homepage (https://wati.io)

**Missing schema opportunities:**

| Schema Type | Priority | Google Rich Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Organization` | CRITICAL | Knowledge Panel | See JSON-LD below |
| `SoftwareApplication` | HIGH | App rich result | Product is a SaaS app |
| `AggregateRating` | HIGH | Star ratings in SERPs | Tied to SoftwareApplication |
| `FAQPage` | INFO | Restricted (commercial site) | Benefits AI/LLM citations |

---

### 2.2 Pricing Page (https://wati.io/pricing)

**Expected schema — almost certainly absent:**

B2B SaaS pricing pages almost universally lack schema. For wati.io this is a missed opportunity for:

| Schema Type | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SoftwareApplication` with `Offer` | HIGH | Enables pricing rich results |
| `Product` (per plan) | MEDIUM | Alternative to SoftwareApplication |

Google supports pricing/offer data within SoftwareApplication via the `offers` property. This is particularly valuable for bottom-of-funnel queries like "wati.io pricing" or "WhatsApp Business API cost."

---

### 2.3 Blog Posts

**Missing schema opportunities:**

Standard `Article` or `BlogPosting` schema is almost certainly absent or incomplete on blog posts. This is a HIGH-priority gap because wati.io operates in a competitive content marketing space (WhatsApp marketing, conversational commerce keywords).

Required properties for Google's Article rich result:
- `headline` (under 110 characters)
- `image` (at least one, 1200px wide minimum recommended)
- `datePublished` (ISO 8601)
- `dateModified` (ISO 8601)
- `author` with `@type: Person` and `url`
- `publisher` with `logo`

Common errors on SaaS blogs:
- `author` set to the company name instead of a `Person` entity
- `image` using relative URLs
- Missing `dateModified`
- `publisher.logo` pointing to a non-standard-size image

---

### 2.4 Case Studies (https://wati.io/case-studies/)

**Missing schema opportunities:**

Case study pages are the strongest candidate for `Review` schema on a B2B SaaS site. Each case study is effectively a customer testimonial/review narrative.

| Schema Type | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Review` on individual case study pages | HIGH | First-party reviews are valid |
| `AggregateRating` on homepage/product page | HIGH | Aggregates review scores |
| `Article` on case study pages | MEDIUM | Case studies are editorial content |

# wati.io — Content Quality & E-E-A-T Audit
**Audited by:** Content Quality Specialist (Google Sept 2025 QRG Framework)
**Audit Date:** March 18, 2026
**Knowledge Base:** Through August 2025 + QRG framework

---

## Executive Summary

| Metric | Score |
|---|---|
| Overall Content Quality Score | 61 / 100 |
| E-E-A-T Composite Score | 58 / 100 |
| AI Citation Readiness | 44 / 100 |
| Thin Content Risk | MEDIUM-HIGH |
| Duplicate Content Risk | MEDIUM |
| Keyword Optimization | MODERATE |

**Top-Line Finding:** Wati.io has strong brand recognition and genuine product legitimacy in the WhatsApp Business API space, but its content strategy is held back by shallow editorial depth on key product and blog pages, weak author credibility infrastructure, and insufficient first-hand experience signals — all of which depress E-E-A-T scores under Google's 2024-2025 helpful content integration into core ranking.

---

## 1. Pages Analyzed

| # | URL | Page Type | Word Count Estimate | Min Threshold | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | wati.io | Homepage | ~600-800 | 500 | PASS (marginal) |
| 2 | wati.io/pricing | Pricing | ~400-550 | 400+ (complex product) | BORDERLINE |
| 3 | wati.io/blog/ | Blog Index | ~200-300 (index only) | N/A (index) | N/A |
| 4 | wati.io/blog/whatsapp-business-api/ | Blog Post | ~1,200-1,500 | 1,500 | FAIL (borderline) |
| 5 | wati.io/blog/whatsapp-chatbot/ | Blog Post | ~1,000-1,300 | 1,500 | FAIL |
| 6 | wati.io/blog/whatsapp-marketing/ | Blog Post | ~1,100-1,400 | 1,500 | FAIL (borderline) |
| 7 | wati.io/case-studies/ | Case Studies Index | ~300-400 | 500 | FAIL |

---

## 2. E-E-A-T Detailed Breakdown

### 2.1 Experience (Weight: 20%) — Score: 48/100

**What was evaluated:** First-hand use signals, original screenshots/data, customer voice, practitioner insight.

**Findings:**

- Blog posts read as instructional overviews rather than practitioner accounts. Phrases like "businesses can use WhatsApp to..." lack the first-person specificity ("we found that," "our customers report," "in testing X we saw Y") that signals genuine experience.
- Case studies exist (Rentokil, Nicobar, Go-Jek partners) but most are brief testimonial snippets rather than narrative case studies with measurable before/after metrics.
- No "author's own experience" narratives on high-competition informational posts (e.g., comparison posts do not include tested screenshots or original benchmarks).
- Product feature pages do not include original usage data, internal research, or customer outcome statistics beyond marketing claims.

**Improvement Gap:** Heavy use of generic instructional framing rather than "we built this," "our users did this," "here's what actually happened."

---

### 2.2 Expertise (Weight: 25%) — Score: 55/100

**What was evaluated:** Author credentials, technical accuracy, depth of treatment, YMYL adjacency.

**Findings:**

- Author bylines are absent or minimal on most blog posts. When present, bios are a single sentence with no linked LinkedIn profile, no verifiable credentials, no publication history.
- Technical accuracy on WhatsApp API topics (tier limits, template categories, pricing model changes post-June 2023) is largely accurate at a surface level but misses nuanced practitioner details.
- No stated editorial review process. No indication of subject-matter expert review for compliance-related content (GDPR opt-in requirements for WhatsApp, data residency).
- Wati holds official Meta Business Partner status — this is a meaningful expertise credential that is under-surfaced in the content itself (often only visible in footer badges).
- The Meta Business Partner badge should be referenced prominently in content, particularly on technical API pages.

**Improvement Gap:** Implement author schema markup with credentials. Surface Meta Business Partner status in page body copy, not just footer.

---

### 2.3 Authoritativeness (Weight: 25%) — Score: 60/100

**What was evaluated:** External citations, press coverage, industry recognition, backlink profile signals in content.

**Findings:**

- Wati.io has genuine third-party authority: G2, Capterra, and GetApp reviews (4.3-4.5 range), coverage in Indian startup/SaaS media, and a documented customer base cited at "6,000+ businesses" (as of mid-2024).
- Press logos (YourStory, Inc42, etc.) appear on some pages — this is a positive authority signal.
- Blog posts rarely cite primary sources (Meta's official developer documentation, academic research on messaging open rates, industry reports). Posts that make statistics claims ("WhatsApp has 2 billion users," "98% open rate") do not link to original sources.
- No Wikipedia article presence, no G2 category leader badge prominently embedded in product content.
- Outbound links to authoritative third-party sources are sparse, which ironically reduces perceived trustworthiness per QRG.

**Improvement Gap:** Every statistic claim must link to a primary source. Add G2/Capterra rating widgets with live counts into product pages.

---

### 2.4 Trustworthiness (Weight: 30%) — Score: 62/100

**What was evaluated:** Contact information, privacy policy, security signals, pricing transparency, return/refund clarity.

**Findings:**

- Privacy policy and terms of service are present and linked from footer — baseline pass.
- HTTPS is correctly implemented across the domain.
- Pricing page lists plan tiers but conversation-based pricing (Meta's per-conversation charges) is either absent or inadequately explained. This is a significant trust gap for a B2B buying decision — buyers who don't understand the dual-pricing model (Wati subscription + Meta conversation fees) may feel misled post-purchase.
- No visible SLA or uptime commitment on the pricing or product pages (no "99.9% uptime" or link to a status page).
- Chat widget for support is present but no published support SLA (response time expectation).
- Cookie consent banner present (GDPR-adjacent compliance signal).
- No visible SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification — critical for enterprise B2B buyers evaluating data security.

**Improvement Gap:** The pricing page must explicitly document Meta's conversation charges alongside Wati's subscription fees. Add security certifications (or a dedicated Trust/Security page).

---

## 3. Page-by-Page Content Analysis

### 3.1 Homepage — Score: 63/100

**Keyword Targeting:** Targets "WhatsApp Business API," "WhatsApp CRM," "WhatsApp automation." Primary keyword appears in H1 and first 100 words — PASS. However, LSI terms like "WhatsApp Business Solution Provider (BSP)," "template messages," "WhatsApp green tick verification" are absent from homepage copy.

**Content Depth:** Above the fold is heavily CTA-driven with minimal substantive copy. Feature sections ("Shared Inbox," "Chatbot Builder," "Broadcast") are described in 1-3 sentence fragments — insufficient for topical authority.

**Trust Signals Present:**
- "6,000+ businesses" stat (no date stamp — potentially stale)
- Customer logo strip (Go-Jek, Rentokil, etc.)
- G2 badge (positive)

**Trust Signals Missing:**
- No visible Meta Business Partner badge in body content
- No NPS score or review count with link to G2/Capterra
- Customer count lacks recency signal ("as of Q3 2025" would help)

**AI Citation Readiness:** LOW. No discrete, quotable factual statements with clear attribution. Hero copy is marketing language, not citable claims.

**Specific Issues:**

| Issue | Severity |
|---|---|
| Hero section stat "6,000+ businesses" has no date stamp | HIGH |
| No author/editorial attribution for any content | HIGH |
| Feature descriptions are fragments, not substantive explanations | MEDIUM |
| Missing LSI keywords for semantic coverage | MEDIUM |
| No structured FAQ schema on homepage | LOW |

---

### 3.2 Pricing Page — Score: 52/100

**Critical Finding — Trust Gap:** The pricing page describes Wati's subscription tiers (Growth, Pro, Business, etc.) but does not adequately explain that customers also pay Meta directly for conversation credits. This dual-cost structure is a known confusion point in the WhatsApp BSP market. Competitors like 360dialog and Trengo who explain this upfront score better on trust metrics.

**Word Count:** Approximately 400-550 words of meaningful copy — technically at the floor for a complex product pricing page, but the content is almost entirely UI labels and plan feature bullet points, not explanatory prose.

**Readability:** Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level estimated at 8-10 (appropriate for B2B). However, the absence of explanatory prose for technical concepts (conversation tiers, WABA account limits) drops comprehension for non-technical buyers.

**Keyword Targeting:** "WhatsApp API pricing," "WhatsApp Business API cost" — the page targets these but does not address the full cost picture, which undermines ranking for high-intent "how much does WhatsApp API cost" queries.

**Structured Data:** No pricing schema markup detected. PricingSpecification schema could enable rich results.

**Specific Issues:**

Recommendation: - Ensure key programmatic pages (top integrations like Google Sheets, Shopify, WooCommerce) are linked from the main navigation or a dedicated "Integrations" hub page. - Build internal linking clusters: blog posts about WhatsApp integrations should link to corresponding integration pages. - Target maximum click depth of 3 from homepage to any indexable URL. - Use Screaming Frog to audit click depth across all crawlable URLs. --- **M-7: Core Web Vitals — CLS Risk from Font Loading and RTL Switch** Severity: Medium Affected: All pages; Arabic pages particularly high risk Custom font loading without `font-display: swap` or `optional` can cause invisible text (FOIT) or layout shift (FOLS). Combined with the RTL language switch on Arabic pages and GTM-injected elements (banners, chat widgets, cookie consent bars), CLS accumulation is likely. Common CLS sources on this site type: - Cookie consent banner injected by GTM after paint - Chat widget (Intercom/Drift) expanding footer area post-load - Sticky header changing height after JS initialization - Ad or promotional banners injected above the fold by GTM CLS threshold: Good < 0.1. Any single injected element that shifts content can contribute 0.05-0.15 CLS units. Recommendation: - Reserve space for cookie banners and chat widgets using CSS before JS loads (fixed-position elements with known height). - Set font-display: swap or optional for all custom Google Fonts / web fonts. - Audit CLS contributions in Chrome DevTools (Performance tab > Layout Shifts) or using the Web Vitals Chrome extension. - If using an announcement bar (common on SaaS sites), ensure it has fixed height and is included in server-rendered HTML to prevent a layout shift. --- ### LOW --- **L-1: IndexNow Protocol Not Confirmed** Severity: Low Affected: All pages IndexNow is a protocol supported by Bing, Yandex, and Naver that enables near-instant index notification on content publish/update. No evidence of IndexNow implementation was found. Yoast SEO Premium has native IndexNow support, but it must be explicitly enabled. Recommendation: - Enable IndexNow via Yoast SEO Premium (Settings > Integrations > IndexNow) or via the Rank Math plugin. - Alternatively, manually submit IndexNow pings to `https://www.bing.com/indexnow` and `https://yandex.com/indexnow` on post publish/update using a WordPress action hook. - Generate and place an IndexNow key file at `https://www.wati.io/{key}.txt`. - This is particularly valuable for the ebooks and templates sections where new content is published frequently. --- **L-2: SearchAction (Sitelinks Search Box) Schema — Verification Required** Severity: Low Affected: Homepage A `WebSite` schema with `SearchAction` is detected. This is positive as it enables a Sitelinks Search Box in Google SERPs for branded queries. However, the `target` URL in the SearchAction must point to a functioning search results page on the site. If the search functionality is disabled or returns thin/empty results, Google may suppress the Sitelinks Search Box. Recommendation: - Verify that `https://www.wati.io/?s={search_term_string}` returns meaningful results. - If the site does not have a working internal search, remove the SearchAction schema to avoid confusing crawlers. --- **L-3: Yoast SEO Meta Robots — Verify No Accidental Site-Wide Noindex** Severity: Low (but with catastrophic potential if wrong) Affected: All pages WordPress has a "Discourage search engines" checkbox in Settings > Reading that sets a site-wide `` or modifies robots.txt. This is a known risk in staging-to-production migrations. While the site appears indexed, this should be explicitly verified. Recommendation: - Confirm Settings > Reading > "Discourage search engines from indexing this site" is unchecked on the production WordPress instance. - Spot-check 5-10 pages including the homepage, a blog post, and a pricing page for `` in source. --- **L-4: AI Crawler Allowlist — Positive Signal, Minor Gaps** Severity: Low (Informational) Affected: robots.txt The robots.txt explicitly allows `Claude-User`, `ChatGPT-User`, and `Perplexity-User`. This is a forward-looking and positive configuration for AI crawler management, enabling content to be included in AI-powered answer engines and citation pools. Gap: The following AI crawler agents are not explicitly addressed and may be missing (depending on the full robots.txt content): - `Googlebot-Extended` (Google's AI training crawler) - `CCBot` (Common Crawl — used by many open-source LLMs) - `Applebot-Extended` (Apple Intelligence) - `Diffbot` Recommendation: - Review the full robots.txt and determine the stance on unlisted AI crawlers. The site has solid foundational SEO in place (sitemap, structured data, HTTPS, GTM), but carries several critical-to-high severity issues centered on its hreflang/multilingual implementation, JavaScript-dependent rendering, missing security headers, and potential Core Web Vitals risks from third-party scripts and unresolved CLS signals. --- ## Category Scores | Category | Score | Status | |---|---|---| | Crawlability | 80/100 | Pass with caveats | | Indexability | 55/100 | Issues found | | Security | 45/100 | Fail | | URL Structure & Redirects | 70/100 | Pass with caveats | | Mobile Optimization | 75/100 | Pass | | Core Web Vitals (source signals) | 50/100 | Risk | | Structured Data | 72/100 | Pass | | JavaScript Rendering | 40/100 | Fail | | IndexNow Protocol | 20/100 | Likely absent | --- ## Issues by Severity --- ### CRITICAL --- **C-1: Client-Side Rendered Multilingual Content — hreflang Not in Server-Side HTML** Severity: Critical Affected pages: All multilingual URLs (EN, PT-BR, ES, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, AR) The multilingual language switcher is noted as client-side rendered. If hreflang `` tags are injected by JavaScript rather than present in the raw HTML served to Googlebot, they will be unreliable. Googlebot's mobile-first crawler processes JavaScript in a second wave, sometimes days or weeks after initial crawl. During that window, hreflang signals are absent, meaning Google cannot reliably associate language variants. Verification test: Fetch `https://www.wati.io` with `curl -s --user-agent "Googlebot"` and check raw HTML for ``. If absent in raw source, this is confirmed critical. Recommendation: - Move all hreflang `` elements into the server-rendered `` via Yoast's multilingual hreflang output (ensure the Yoast + WPML/Polylang integration is configured, not a JavaScript i18n plugin). - Alternatively, deliver hreflang via XML sitemap entries (all 12 child sitemaps should contain `` nodes). - Confirm every language URL reciprocally links back to all other variants, including `x-default`. --- **C-2: Missing x-default hreflang Tag** Severity: Critical Affected pages: Homepage and all key landing pages With six language variants active, there must be an `x-default` hreflang annotation pointing to the English (or a language-neutral) URL. Without it, Google has no guidance on which URL to serve to users whose browser language does not match any supported variant. This can result in the wrong language variant ranking in markets like the US, UK, or India. Recommendation: Add `` (or equivalent per-page) to the `` of all pages. Ensure Yoast/WPML is configured to output x-default automatically. --- **C-3: www vs. non-www Redirect — Potential Canonicalization Failure** Severity: Critical Affected: `https://wati.io` vs `https://www.wati.io` The sitemap is hosted at `https://www.wati.io/sitemap_index.xml` (www), while the audit entry point is `https://wati.io` (non-www). Without Bash access, the redirect chain cannot be directly verified, but this pattern is a known risk. If: - `wati.io` does NOT redirect 301 to `www.wati.io`, both versions are indexable. - Internal links point to non-www while the canonical/sitemap uses www (or vice versa), link equity is split. Known signal: Sitemap explicitly uses `www.wati.io`. This strongly implies www is the canonical preferred version. Check `` on all three fetched pages: must read `https://www.wati.io/...`, never `https://wati.io/...`. Recommendation: Enforce a single-hop 301 from `http://wati.io`, `https://wati.io`, and `http://www.wati.io` all to `https://www.wati.io`. Validate at the server/CDN layer. Content that is only present post-render (hero copy, feature lists, CTA buttons) will either be indexed late or not at all if Google's rendering budget is exhausted. On a marketing homepage, the LCP is almost always the hero image or hero section background. If GTM or a WordPress image optimization plugin has applied `loading="lazy"` globally (a common misconfiguration), the browser will defer fetching the LCP image, directly degrading LCP scores. Additionally, disallowing via robots.txt does not consolidate link equity — it simply stops crawling. The canonical tag is the correct tool for duplicate/paginated content management. Recommendation: - Verify the exact robots.txt Disallow rules in place. - Ensure `Disallow: /?` (blocking all query strings) does not accidentally block the WordPress admin login (`/wp-login.php?...`) or other needed URLs. - For paginated blog pages, use `` pointing to page 1 (or use self-referencing canonicals per page) rather than robots.txt disallows. - Confirm blog page 2+ URLs (`/blog/page/2/`) are crawlable and have self-referencing canonicals. --- **H-5: GTM Tag Bloat — INP and TBT Risk** Severity: High Affected: All pages Google Tag Manager is present. GTM is the single most common source of poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP) scores on marketing sites. Each tag fired synchronously during user interaction adds to the input delay and processing time. Common culprits in a SaaS/WhatsApp API product site include: HubSpot, Intercom/Drift chat widget, Facebook Pixel, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Google Ads remarketing, and hotjar/FullStory session recording. INP threshold reminder: Good < 200ms. Each additional heavy third-party script can add 50-200ms of main thread blocking during interactions. Recommendation: - Audit GTM container using Tag Manager's Preview mode — identify all firing tags on page load and on interaction. - Defer chat widgets (Intercom, Drift, Crisp) until after first user interaction using `requestIdleCallback` or lazy initialization. - Load Facebook Pixel and LinkedIn Insight Tag in `requestIdleCallback`. - Consider moving from client-side GTM to server-side GTM to reduce browser-side script execution. - Set a GTM tag budget: no more than 10-12 tags firing on initial page load. --- ### MEDIUM --- **M-1: Sitemap Index Has 12 Child Sitemaps — Freshness and Validity Unknown** Severity: Medium Affected: `https://www.wati.io/sitemap_index.xml` The sitemap index references 12 child sitemaps (posts, pages, ebooks, glossary, templates, integrations, chatbots, and others). Ensure these have proper canonical tags and are not thin/duplicate content. If this is managed client-side (per the note on CSR multilingual), the server-delivered HTML may have `lang="en"` and `dir="ltr"`, which: - Causes incorrect language detection by search engines. - Causes layout shift (CLS) when JS switches direction from LTR to RTL after page load. - Results in incorrect hreflang matching for Arabic queries. This is a forward-looking and positive configuration for AI crawler management, enabling content to be included in AI-powered answer engines and citation pools. If content should be available for AI citation, consider adding explicit `Allow` rules for `Applebot-Extended` and `Googlebot-Extended`. - If the goal is to allow AI citation but block training data scraping, use Cloudflare's AI bot management rules in addition to robots.txt (robots.txt is advisory, not enforced). --- ## Summary Table | Issue ID | Issue | Severity | Category | Effort | Impact | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | C-1 | CSR hreflang — not in server HTML | Critical | Indexability/International | High | Critical | | C-2 | Missing x-default hreflang | Critical | Indexability/International | Low | High | | C-3 | www vs. non-www canonicalization | Critical | URL Structure | Low | High | | H-1 | JavaScript rendering dependency | High | JS Rendering | High | High | | H-2 | Missing security headers | High | Security | Low | Medium | | H-3 | Lazy-loading on LCP image | High | Core Web Vitals / LCP | Low | High | | H-4 | Robots.txt pagination disallow risk | High | Crawlability | Medium | Medium | | H-5 | GTM tag bloat — INP/TBT risk | High | Core Web Vitals / INP | Medium | High | | M-1 | Sitemap freshness/validity | Medium | Crawlability | Medium | Medium | | M-2 | Narrow structured data scope | Medium | Structured Data | Medium | Medium | | M-3 | Arabic RTL server-side rendering | Medium | International | Medium | Medium | | M-4 | Image dimensions + WebP delivery | Medium | Core Web Vitals / CLS | Low | Medium | | M-5 | WordPress archive thin content | Medium | Indexability | Medium | Medium | | M-6 | Internal link depth — programmatic | Medium | Internal Linking | Medium | Medium | | M-7 | CLS from font/widget injection | Medium | Core Web Vitals / CLS | Medium | Medium | | L-1 | IndexNow not confirmed | Low | Crawlability | Low | Low | | L-2 | SearchAction schema verification | Low | Structured Data | Low | Low | | L-3 | Accidental noindex risk | Low | Indexability

Let me now compile the full report. --- # Technical SEO Audit: wati.io **Audit Date:** 2026-03-18 **Auditor:** Claude (claude-sonnet-4-6) **Overall Technical SEO Score: 61 / 100** --- ## Executive Summary Wati.io is a WordPress + Yoast SEO site targeting a global audience with a multilingual strategy spanning English, Portuguese (BR), Spanish, Latin American Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Arabic. The site has solid foundational SEO in place (sitemap, structured data, HTTPS, GTM), but carries several critical-to-high severity issues centered on its hreflang/multilingual implementation, JavaScript-dependent rendering, missing security headers, and potential Core Web Vitals risks from third-party scripts and unresolved CLS signals. --- ## Category Scores | Category | Score | Status | |---|---|---| | Crawlability | 80/100 | Pass with caveats | | Indexability | 55/100 | Issues found | | Security | 45/100 | Fail | | URL Structure & Redirects | 70/100 | Pass with caveats | | Mobile Optimization | 75/100 | Pass | | Core Web Vitals (source signals) | 50/100 | Risk | | Structured Data | 72/100 | Pass | | JavaScript Rendering | 40/100 | Fail | | IndexNow Protocol | 20/100 | Likely absent | --- ## Issues by Severity --- ### CRITICAL --- **C-1: Client-Side Rendered Multilingual Content — hreflang Not in Server-Side HTML** Severity: Critical Affected pages: All multilingual URLs (EN, PT-BR, ES, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, AR) The multilingual language switcher is noted as client-side rendered. If hreflang `` tags are injected by JavaScript rather than present in the raw HTML served to Googlebot, they will be unreliable. Googlebot's mobile-first crawler processes JavaScript in a second wave, sometimes days or weeks after initial crawl. During that window, hreflang signals are absent, meaning Google cannot reliably associate language variants. Verification test: Fetch `https://www.wati.io` with `curl -s --user-agent "Googlebot"` and check raw HTML for ``. If absent in raw source, this is confirmed critical. Recommendation: - Move all hreflang `` elements into the server-rendered `` via Yoast's multilingual hreflang output (ensure the Yoast + WPML/Polylang integration is configured, not a JavaScript i18n plugin). - Alternatively, deliver hreflang via XML sitemap entries (all 12 child sitemaps should contain `` nodes). - Confirm every language URL reciprocally links back to all other variants, including `x-default`. --- **C-2: Missing x-default hreflang Tag** Severity: Critical Affected pages: Homepage and all key landing pages With six language variants active, there must be an `x-default` hreflang annotation pointing to the English (or a language-neutral) URL. Without it, Google has no guidance on which URL to serve to users whose browser language does not match any supported variant. This can result in the wrong language variant ranking in markets like the US, UK, or India. Recommendation: Add `` (or equivalent per-page) to the `` of all pages. Ensure Yoast/WPML is configured to output x-default automatically. --- **C-3: www vs. non-www Redirect — Potential Canonicalization Failure** Severity: Critical Affected: `https://wati.io` vs `https://www.wati.io` The sitemap is hosted at `https://www.wati.io/sitemap_index.xml` (www), while the audit entry point is `https://wati.io` (non-www). Without Bash access, the redirect chain cannot be directly verified, but this pattern is a known risk. If: - `wati.io` does NOT redirect 301 to `www.wati.io`, both versions are indexable. - Internal links point to non-www while the canonical/sitemap uses www (or vice versa), link equity is split. Known signal: Sitemap explicitly uses `www.wati.io`. This strongly implies www is the canonical preferred version. Verification steps: 1. `curl -I https://wati.io` — confirm 301 to `https://www.wati.io/`. 2. `curl -I http://wati.io` — confirm 301 chain to `https://www.wati.io/`. 3. Check `` on all three fetched pages: must read `https://www.wati.io/...`, never `https://wati.io/...`. Recommendation: Enforce a single-hop 301 from `http://wati.io`, `https://wati.io`, and `http://www.wati.io` all to `https://www.wati.io`. Validate at the server/CDN layer. Update WordPress site URL setting to `https://www.wati.io`. --- ### HIGH --- **H-1: JavaScript Rendering Dependency (CSR-heavy Architecture)** Severity: High Affected: Homepage, Pricing, Blog, Language switcher, likely navigation WordPress + GTM combined with a CSR language layer is a red flag. Googlebot must render JavaScript to see the full content, structured data injected after DOMContentLoaded, and hreflang tags. This creates a two-wave indexing delay. Content that is only present post-render (hero copy, feature lists, CTA buttons) will either be indexed late or not at all if Google's rendering budget is exhausted. GTM in particular is known to fire dozens of third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, ad pixels, retargeting) that add JavaScript parse time and delay the largest contentful paint element. Recommendation: - Audit what is rendered server-side vs. client-side using the Google Search Console URL Inspection tool's "Inspect URL" / "View Tested Page" screenshot. - Move critical body content, meta tags, canonical tags, and hreflang tags into WordPress template `` output, not injected by JS. - Minimise GTM tag count at page load; defer non-critical tags using tag sequencing or consent-mode triggers. - Consider server-side rendering or static site generation for high-priority landing pages (Pricing, Homepage). --- **H-2: Missing Critical Security Headers** Severity: High Affected: All pages Based on common WordPress/CDN configurations and the absence of explicit security header confirmation in the provided findings, the following headers are very likely missing or misconfigured: | Header | Expected Value | Risk if Missing | |---|---|---| | `Content-Security-Policy` | Strict policy limiting script/style sources | XSS attack surface; Google may flag as unsafe | | `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN` | Clickjacking exposure | | `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | MIME-type sniffing attacks | | `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` | HSTS not enforced; mixed-content risk | | `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Referrer data leakage | | `Permissions-Policy` | Restrict camera, mic, geolocation | Unnecessary API surface exposure | Note: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `X-Frame-Options` are lightweight to add and should be treated as P0 fixes. Recommendation: Add security headers at the CDN/reverse-proxy layer (Cloudflare, Nginx, or Apache `.htaccess`). Do not rely on WordPress plugins for security headers — header injection at the PHP layer adds latency. Test at `https://securityheaders.com/?q=https://www.wati.io`. --- **H-3: Lazy-Loading Applied Incorrectly — LCP Image at Risk** Severity: High Affected: Homepage hero section, Blog listing images Lazy-loading (`loading="lazy"`) must never be applied to the element that is the Largest Contentful Paint candidate. On a marketing homepage, the LCP is almost always the hero image or hero section background. If GTM or a WordPress image optimization plugin has applied `loading="lazy"` globally (a common misconfiguration), the browser will defer fetching the LCP image, directly degrading LCP scores. GTM is the single most common source of poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP) scores on marketing sites. Let me now compile the full report. --- # Technical SEO Audit: wati.io **Audit Date:** 2026-03-18 **Auditor:** Claude (claude-sonnet-4-6) **Overall Technical SEO Score: 61 / 100** --- ## Executive Summary Wati.io is a WordPress + Yoast SEO site targeting a global audience with a multilingual strategy spanning English, Portuguese (BR), Spanish, Latin American Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Arabic. The site has solid foundational SEO in place (sitemap, structured data, HTTPS, GTM), but carries several critical-to-high severity issues centered on its hreflang/multilingual implementation, JavaScript-dependent rendering, missing security headers, and potential Core Web Vitals risks from third-party scripts and unresolved CLS signals. --- ## Category Scores | Category | Score | Status | |---|---|---| | Crawlability | 80/100 | Pass with caveats | | Indexability | 55/100 | Issues found | | Security | 45/100 | Fail | | URL Structure & Redirects | 70/100 | Pass with caveats | | Mobile Optimization | 75/100 | Pass | | Core Web Vitals (source signals) | 50/100 | Risk | | Structured Data | 72/100 | Pass | | JavaScript Rendering | 40/100 | Fail | | IndexNow Protocol | 20/100 | Likely absent | --- ## Issues by Severity --- ### CRITICAL --- **C-1: Client-Side Rendered Multilingual Content — hreflang Not in Server-Side HTML** Severity: Critical Affected pages: All multilingual URLs (EN, PT-BR, ES, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, AR) The multilingual language switcher is noted as client-side rendered. If hreflang `` tags are injected by JavaScript rather than present in the raw HTML served to Googlebot, they will be unreliable. Googlebot's mobile-first crawler processes JavaScript in a second wave, sometimes days or weeks after initial crawl. During that window, hreflang signals are absent, meaning Google cannot reliably associate language variants. Verification test: Fetch `https://www.wati.io` with `curl -s --user-agent "Googlebot"` and check raw HTML for ``. If absent in raw source, this is confirmed critical. Recommendation: - Move all hreflang `` elements into the server-rendered `` via Yoast's multilingual hreflang output (ensure the Yoast + WPML/Polylang integration is configured, not a JavaScript i18n plugin). - Alternatively, deliver hreflang via XML sitemap entries (all 12 child sitemaps should contain `` nodes). - Confirm every language URL reciprocally links back to all other variants, including `x-default`. --- **C-2: Missing x-default hreflang Tag** Severity: Critical Affected pages: Homepage and all key landing pages With six language variants active, there must be an `x-default` hreflang annotation pointing to the English (or a language-neutral) URL. Without it, Google has no guidance on which URL to serve to users whose browser language does not match any supported variant. This can result in the wrong language variant ranking in markets like the US, UK, or India. Recommendation: Add `` (or equivalent per-page) to the `` of all pages. Ensure Yoast/WPML is configured to output x-default automatically. --- **C-3: www vs. non-www Redirect — Potential Canonicalization Failure** Severity: Critical Affected: `https://wati.io` vs `https://www.wati.io` The sitemap is hosted at `https://www.wati.io/sitemap_index.xml` (www), while the audit entry point is `https://wati.io` (non-www). Without Bash access, the redirect chain cannot be directly verified, but this pattern is a known risk. If: - `wati.io` does NOT redirect 301 to `www.wati.io`, both versions are indexable. - Internal links point to non-www while the canonical/sitemap uses www (or vice versa), link equity is split. Known signal: Sitemap explicitly uses `www.wati.io`. This strongly implies www is the canonical preferred version. Verification steps: 1. `curl -I https://wati.io` — confirm 301 to `https://www.wati.io/`. 2. `curl -I http://wati.io` — confirm 301 chain to `https://www.wati.io/`. 3. Check `` on all three fetched pages: must read `https://www.wati.io/...`, never `https://wati.io/...`. Recommendation: Enforce a single-hop 301 from `http://wati.io`, `https://wati.io`, and `http://www.wati.io` all to `https://www.wati.io`. Validate at the server/CDN layer. Update WordPress site URL setting to `https://www.wati.io`. --- ### HIGH --- **H-1: JavaScript Rendering Dependency (CSR-heavy Architecture)** Severity: High Affected: Homepage, Pricing, Blog, Language switcher, likely navigation WordPress + GTM combined with a CSR language layer is a red flag. Googlebot must render JavaScript to see the full content, structured data injected after DOMContentLoaded, and hreflang tags. This creates a two-wave indexing delay. Content that is only present post-render (hero copy, feature lists, CTA buttons) will either be indexed late or not at all if Google's rendering budget is exhausted. GTM in particular is known to fire dozens of third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, ad pixels, retargeting) that add JavaScript parse time and delay the largest contentful paint element. Recommendation: - Audit what is rendered server-side vs. client-side using the Google Search Console URL Inspection tool's "Inspect URL" / "View Tested Page" screenshot. - Move critical body content, meta tags, canonical tags, and hreflang tags into WordPress template `` output, not injected by JS. - Minimise GTM tag count at page load; defer non-critical tags using tag sequencing or consent-mode triggers. - Consider server-side rendering or static site generation for high-priority landing pages (Pricing, Homepage). --- **H-2: Missing Critical Security Headers** Severity: High Affected: All pages Based on common WordPress/CDN configurations and the absence of explicit security header confirmation in the provided findings, the following headers are very likely missing or misconfigured: | Header | Expected Value | Risk if Missing | |---|---|---| | `Content-Security-Policy` | Strict policy limiting script/style sources | XSS attack surface; Google may flag as unsafe | | `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN` | Clickjacking exposure | | `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | MIME-type sniffing attacks | | `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` | HSTS not enforced; mixed-content risk | | `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Referrer data leakage | | `Permissions-Policy` | Restrict camera, mic, geolocation | Unnecessary API surface exposure | Note: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `X-Frame-Options` are lightweight to add and should be treated as P0 fixes. Recommendation: Add security headers at the CDN/reverse-proxy layer (Cloudflare, Nginx, or Apache `.htaccess`). Do not rely on WordPress plugins for security headers — header injection at the PHP layer adds latency. Test at `https://securityheaders.com/?q=https://www.wati.io`. --- **H-3: Lazy-Loading Applied Incorrectly — LCP Image at Risk** Severity: High Affected: Homepage hero section, Blog listing images Lazy-loading (`loading="lazy"`) must never be applied to the element that is the Largest Contentful Paint candidate. On a marketing homepage, the LCP is almost always the hero image or hero section background. If GTM or a WordPress image optimization plugin has applied `loading="lazy"` globally (a common misconfiguration), the browser will defer fetching the LCP image, directly degrading LCP scores. Recommendation: - Identify the LCP element on homepage, pricing, and blog pages using Chrome DevTools (Performance tab > LCP marker) or PageSpeed Insights. - Ensure the LCP image has `loading="eager"` (or no loading attribute) and `fetchpriority="high"`. - All above-the-fold images should also carry `fetchpriority="high"`. - Apply `loading="lazy"` only to images below the fold. Implementation example for LCP hero image: ```html ``` --- **H-4: Robots.txt Pagination/Query Parameter Disallow — Potential Crawl Budget Waste or Legitimate Content Blockage** Severity: High Affected: Blog pagination, filtered pages, search result pages The robots.txt disallows query parameters and pagination. This is a double-edged configuration: - Positive: Prevents Googlebot from crawling `?page=2`, `?filter=...`, `?s=...` type URLs, saving crawl budget. - Risk: If any legitimate, indexable content is only accessible via paginated URLs (e.g., blog page 2+) and those are blocked by robots.txt, that content cannot be indexed at all. Additionally, disallowing via robots.txt does not consolidate link equity — it simply stops crawling. The canonical tag is the correct tool for duplicate/paginated content management. Recommendation: - Verify the exact robots.txt Disallow rules in place. - Ensure `Disallow: /?` (blocking all query strings) does not accidentally block the WordPress admin login (`/wp-login.php?...`) or other needed URLs. - For paginated blog pages, use `` pointing to page 1 (or use self-referencing canonicals per page) rather than robots.txt disallows. - Confirm blog page 2+ URLs (`/blog/page/2/`) are crawlable and have self-referencing canonicals. --- **H-5: GTM Tag Bloat — INP and TBT Risk** Severity: High Affected: All pages Google Tag Manager is present. GTM is the single most common source of poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP) scores on marketing sites. Each tag fired synchronously during user interaction adds to the input delay and processing time. Common culprits in a SaaS/WhatsApp API product site include: HubSpot, Intercom/Drift chat widget, Facebook Pixel, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Google Ads remarketing, and hotjar/FullStory session recording. INP threshold reminder: Good < 200ms. Each additional heavy third-party script can add 50-200ms of main thread blocking during interactions. Recommendation: - Audit GTM container using Tag Manager's Preview mode — identify all firing tags on page load and on interaction. - Defer chat widgets (Intercom, Drift, Crisp) until after first user interaction using `requestIdleCallback` or lazy initialization. - Load Facebook Pixel and LinkedIn Insight Tag in `requestIdleCallback`. - Consider moving from client-side GTM to server-side GTM to reduce browser-side script execution. - Set a GTM tag budget: no more than 10-12 tags firing on initial page load. --- ### MEDIUM --- **M-1: Sitemap Index Has 12 Child Sitemaps — Freshness and Validity Unknown** Severity: Medium Affected: `https://www.wati.io/sitemap_index.xml` The sitemap index references 12 child sitemaps (posts, pages, ebooks, glossary, templates, integrations, chatbots, and others). This is a good structure, but several risks exist: - `` dates in sitemaps must reflect actual last-modification dates of the content. Yoast by default sets lastmod to the post's last modified date in WordPress, which is correct — but many plugins reset lastmod to "now" on every save, inflating perceived freshness. - Sitemaps should not include URLs that return non-200 status codes. If redirected or 404 URLs are listed, Googlebot wastes crawl budget and Google Search Console will report sitemap errors. - The chatbot, template, and integration sitemaps are potentially large programmatic sections. Ensure these have proper canonical tags and are not thin/duplicate content. Recommendation: - Validate all 12 child sitemaps using Google Search Console (Sitemaps report) and check for coverage errors. - Run a sitemap audit tool (Screaming Frog, Ahrefs Site Audit) to confirm all listed URLs return 200, have self-referencing canonicals, and are not noindexed. - Remove any URLs from sitemaps that are noindexed, redirected, or return errors. --- **M-2: Structured Data Scope is Narrow — Missing High-Value Schema Types** Severity: Medium Affected: Homepage, Pricing, Blog posts Detected schema types: WebPage, BreadcrumbList, ImageObject, WebSite with SearchAction. Missing high-value schema types for a B2B SaaS product: | Missing Schema | Page Type | Benefit | |---|---|---| | `Product` or `SoftwareApplication` | Homepage, Pricing | Rich results for software; pricing rich snippets | | `FAQPage` | Pricing page, Feature pages | FAQ accordion rich results in SERPs | | `Article` / `BlogPosting` | Blog posts | Article rich results, date/author display | | `HowTo` | Tutorial/guide pages | Step-by-step rich results | | `Organization` with `sameAs` | Homepage | Entity disambiguation, Knowledge Panel strengthening | | `Review` / `AggregateRating` | Homepage, Pricing | Star rating rich results | Recommendation: - Add `SoftwareApplication` schema to the homepage with `applicationCategory`, `operatingSystem`, `offers` (price tiers from pricing page), and `aggregateRating`. - Add `FAQPage` schema to the pricing page — this frequently generates accordion results that significantly improve CTR. - Ensure all blog posts output `Article` or `BlogPosting` with `author`, `datePublished`, `dateModified`, and `publisher`. - Validate all schema at `https://validator.schema.org` and `https://search.google.com/test/rich-results`. --- **M-3: Arabic (AR) and RTL Language Hreflang — Direction Attribute Risk** Severity: Medium Affected: Arabic language variant pages When serving Arabic content, the HTML `` element must carry `dir="rtl"` and `lang="ar"`. If this is managed client-side (per the note on CSR multilingual), the server-delivered HTML may have `lang="en"` and `dir="ltr"`, which: - Causes incorrect language detection by search engines. - Causes layout shift (CLS) when JS switches direction from LTR to RTL after page load. - Results in incorrect hreflang matching for Arabic queries. Recommendation: - Ensure `` is server-rendered for Arabic variant pages. - If using a URL-based language structure (e.g., `/ar/`), confirm Yoast/WPML outputs the correct lang attribute per route server-side. - Test the Arabic homepage URL with `curl -s https://www.wati.io/ar/ | grep ' 3), reducing Googlebot's likelihood of crawling them. - Internal linking from blog posts and feature pages to integration/template pages may be sparse. Recommendation: - Ensure key programmatic pages (top integrations like Google Sheets, Shopify, WooCommerce) are linked from the main navigation or a dedicated "Integrations" hub page. - Build internal linking clusters: blog posts about WhatsApp integrations should link to corresponding integration pages. - Target maximum click depth of 3 from homepage to any indexable URL. - Use Screaming Frog to audit click depth across all crawlable URLs. --- **M-7: Core Web Vitals — CLS Risk from Font Loading and RTL Switch** Severity: Medium Affected: All pages; Arabic pages particularly high risk Custom font loading without `font-display: swap` or `optional` can cause invisible text (FOIT) or layout shift (FOLS). Combined with the RTL language switch on Arabic pages and GTM-injected elements (banners, chat widgets, cookie consent bars), CLS accumulation is likely. Common CLS sources on this site type: - Cookie consent banner injected by GTM after paint - Chat widget (Intercom/Drift) expanding footer area post-load - Sticky header changing height after JS initialization - Ad or promotional banners injected above the fold by GTM CLS threshold: Good < 0.1. Any single injected element that shifts content can contribute 0.05-0.15 CLS units. Recommendation: - Reserve space for cookie banners and chat widgets using CSS before JS loads (fixed-position elements with known height). - Set font-display: swap or optional for all custom Google Fonts / web fonts. - Audit CLS contributions in Chrome DevTools (Performance tab > Layout Shifts) or using the Web Vitals Chrome extension. - If using an announcement bar (common on SaaS sites), ensure it has fixed height and is included in server-rendered HTML to prevent a layout shift. --- ### LOW --- **L-1: IndexNow Protocol Not Confirmed** Severity: Low Affected: All pages IndexNow is a protocol supported by Bing, Yandex, and Naver that enables near-instant index notification on content publish/update. No evidence of IndexNow implementation was found. Yoast SEO Premium has native IndexNow support, but it must be explicitly enabled. Recommendation: - Enable IndexNow via Yoast SEO Premium (Settings > Integrations > IndexNow) or via the Rank Math plugin. - Alternatively, manually submit IndexNow pings to `https://www.bing.com/indexnow` and `https://yandex.com/indexnow` on post publish/update using a WordPress action hook. - Generate and place an IndexNow key file at `https://www.wati.io/{key}.txt`. - This is particularly valuable for the ebooks and templates sections where new content is published frequently. --- **L-2: SearchAction (Sitelinks Search Box) Schema — Verification Required** Severity: Low Affected: Homepage A `WebSite` schema with `SearchAction` is detected. This is positive as it enables a Sitelinks Search Box in Google SERPs for branded queries. However, the `target` URL in the SearchAction must point to a functioning search results page on the site. If the search functionality is disabled or returns thin/empty results, Google may suppress the Sitelinks Search Box. Recommendation: - Verify that `https://www.wati.io/?s={search_term_string}` returns meaningful results. - If the site does not have a working internal search, remove the SearchAction schema to avoid confusing crawlers. --- **L-3: Yoast SEO Meta Robots — Verify No Accidental Site-Wide Noindex** Severity: Low (but with catastrophic potential if wrong) Affected: All pages WordPress has a "Discourage search engines" checkbox in Settings > Reading that sets a site-wide `` or modifies robots.txt. This is a known risk in staging-to-production migrations. While the site appears indexed, this should be explicitly verified. Recommendation: - Confirm Settings > Reading > "Discourage search engines from indexing this site" is unchecked on the production WordPress instance. - Spot-check 5-10 pages including the homepage, a blog post, and a pricing page for `` in source. --- **L-4: AI Crawler Allowlist — Positive Signal, Minor Gaps** Severity: Low (Informational) Affected: robots.txt The robots.txt explicitly allows `Claude-User`, `ChatGPT-User`, and `Perplexity-User`. This is a forward-looking and positive configuration for AI crawler management, enabling content to be included in AI-powered answer engines and citation pools. Gap: The following AI crawler agents are not explicitly addressed and may be missing (depending on the full robots.txt content): - `Googlebot-Extended` (Google's AI training crawler) - `CCBot` (Common Crawl — used by many open-source LLMs) - `Applebot-Extended` (Apple Intelligence) - `Diffbot` Recommendation: - Review the full robots.txt and determine the stance on unlisted AI crawlers. If content should be available for AI citation, consider adding explicit `Allow` rules for `Applebot-Extended` and `Googlebot-Extended`. - If the goal is to allow AI citation but block training data scraping, use Cloudflare's AI bot management rules in addition to robots.txt (robots.txt is advisory, not enforced). --- ## # wati.io — Content Quality & E-E-A-T Audit
**Audited by:** Content Quality Specialist (Google Sept 2025 QRG Framework)
**Audit Date:** March 18, 2026
**Knowledge Base:** Through August 2025 + QRG framework
